text: Our group project is due this weekend and the GPU cluster queue has been stuck for hours, so none of my runs are even starting.
label: No physio
response: That sounds frustrating. It's understandable that you're feeling frustrated because you're eager to get started, but the cluster is not cooperating. It's not a reflection of your ability to work with the cluster. It's a technical issue that can be fixed.

text: I keep refreshing the queue every ten minutes instead of studying for my other courses, and I know it is not helping.
label: No physio
response: That's a very common pattern. When we're waiting for something to happen, we often end up doing something else instead of what we really want to do. It's not that you're not capable of studying—it's that your mind keeps switching between different expectations.

text: I have barely slept this week and I am starting to make small mistakes in my code that I would never normally make.
label: No physio
response: That sounds like a very stressful situation. When you're exhausted, your mind can't focus properly, and small mistakes can become much more noticeable. It's not that you're not capable of doing your job—it's that your mind is not functioning at its best.

text: Part of me feels like if this does not work out, all the effort I put in this semester was for nothing.
label: No physio
response: That fear is understandable. When you've invested so much time and energy into something, it's natural to worry about whether it was worth it. But it's important to remember that every experience, whether it succeeds or fails, teaches you something. Even if this internship doesn't lead to a job, it has already given you valuable skills, connections, and a clearer idea of what you want.

text: I told a friend about it and they said I am overthinking, but it does not feel that simple to me.
label: No physio
response: I can understand why that feels confusing. When something keeps bothering you, it's natural to feel like you're overthinking. But overthinking often comes from a place of genuine concern, not just a habit. It sounds like you're trying to protect yourself from something that feels important, even if it doesn't feel like it's under control.

text: I think I need to accept that some of this is out of my control and focus on what I can actually finish.
label: No physio
response: That sounds like a realistic and compassionate approach. When we're carrying so much responsibility, it's easy to feel like everything is falling apart, but it's often the small, manageable tasks that give us the most sense of control.

text: Thanks, I feel a bit calmer now. I am going to sleep tonight and look at it fresh tomorrow.
label: No physio
response: That sounds like a good plan. Sometimes the hardest part is getting started, and once you begin, the work itself can help you feel more in control. Tomorrow, you can come back to the problem with a fresh mind and a clearer sense of direction.
